profile.summary: ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 (ProtT5-XL-U50, often just ProtT5) is a protein language model from the ProtTrans project. It reads a single amino acid sequence, with no alignment, and produces a 1024-value embedding for each residue, which can be averaged into one embedding per protein. These embeddings are used as features for downstream predictors, or the model is fine-tuned, for tasks such as secondary structure and subcellular localisation.

summary_quotes.text: Example for how to derive embeddings from our best-performing protein language model, ProtT5-XL-U50 (aka ProtT5)
The model could be used for protein feature extraction or to be fine-tuned on downstream tasks.
We validated the advantage of using the embeddings as exclusive input for several subsequent tasks.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 is based on the t5-3b encoder-decoder model and was pretrained self-supervised on raw protein sequences. Unlike the original T5, which used span denoising, it was trained with a BART-like masked language modelling objective: 15% of amino acids are masked, 90% of those replaced by a mask token and 10% by a different random amino acid. Sequences are uppercased, rare amino acids U, Z, O and B are mapped to X, and each residue is one token. The configuration has 24 layers, hidden size 1024 and 32 attention heads. For feature extraction the developers recommend the encoder output rather than the decoder.
sections.source_locator: Model card: Model description, Preprocessing, Intended uses; config.json

quotes.text: ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 is based on the `t5-3b` model and was pretrained on a large corpus of protein sequences in a self-supervised fashion.
The original T5-3B model was pretrained using a span denosing objective, while this model was pre-trained with a Bart-like MLM denosing objective.
- In 90% of the cases, the masked amino acids are replaced by `[MASK]` token.
The protein sequences are uppercased and tokenized using a single space and a vocabulary size of 21. The rare amino acids "U,Z,O,B" were mapped to "X".
We have also noticed that for feature extraction, its better to use the feature extracted from the encoder not from the decoder.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two Hugging Face checkpoints hold ProtT5-XL-UniRef50: the full encoder-decoder model (Rostlab/prot_t5_xl_uniref50) and an encoder-only half-precision copy (Rostlab/prot_t5_xl_half_uniref50-enc), which the README's quick start uses. The developers report the same downstream performance from both. Sibling ProtT5 models trained on BFD, and XXL variants, are separate checkpoints. ProtT5-XL-UniRef50 was initialised from ProtT5-XL-BFD rather than trained from scratch. A result should name the checkpoint, its revision (this page read 973be27c and 94a6abc0) and whether the encoder output was used.

strengths.text: Needs only the single sequence, not an alignment; the authors say ProtT5 embeddings outperformed earlier methods on per-residue prediction without evolutionary information.

quotes.text: For the per-residue predictions the transfer of the most informative embeddings (ProtT5) for the first time outperformed the state-of-the-art without using evolutionary information thereby bypassing expensive database searches.

strengths.text: The encoder-only half-precision checkpoint runs in 8 GB of GPU memory, and the developers report no measurable loss in performance from it.

run_guide.summary: Install transformers and extract per-residue and per-protein ProtT5 embeddings for two example sequences with the encoder-only half-precision checkpoint.
prerequisites: Python with pip. The sources read do not pin a Python or library version.
A GPU is recommended: the half-precision model runs only on GPU, and the encoder-only checkpoint is stated to be usable on 8 GB of video RAM. On CPU the snippet casts the model to full precision.
Weights are under the Academic Free License v3.0; code is MIT. The weights are not gated.

steps.shell:

pip install transformers
pip install sentencepiece

steps.explanation: The README's install commands. protobuf is the README's fix for a T5 tokenizer error in recent transformers versions.

steps.title: Extract embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
from transformers import T5Tokenizer, T5EncoderModel
import torch
import re

device = torch.device('cuda:0' if torch.cuda.is_available() else 'cpu')

# Load the tokenizer
tokenizer = T5Tokenizer.from_pretrained('Rostlab/prot_t5_xl_half_uniref50-enc', do_lower_case=False)

# Load the model
model = T5EncoderModel.from_pretrained("Rostlab/prot_t5_xl_half_uniref50-enc").to(device)

# only GPUs support half-precision currently; if you want to run on CPU use full-precision (not recommended, much slower)
if device == torch.device("cpu"):
    model.to(torch.float32)

# prepare your protein sequences as a list
sequence_examples = ["PRTEINO", "SEQWENCE"]

# replace all rare/ambiguous amino acids by X and introduce white-space between all amino acids
sequence_examples = [" ".join(list(re.sub(r"[UZOB]", "X", sequence))) for sequence in sequence_examples]

# tokenize sequences and pad up to the longest sequence in the batch
ids = tokenizer(sequence_examples, add_special_tokens=True, padding="longest")

input_ids = torch.tensor(ids['input_ids']).to(device)
attention_mask = torch.tensor(ids['attention_mask']).to(device)

# generate embeddings
with torch.no_grad():
    embedding_repr = model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)

# extract residue embeddings for the first ([0,:]) sequence in the batch and remove padded & special tokens ([0,:7]) 
emb_0 = embedding_repr.last_hidden_state[0,:7] # shape (7 x 1024)
# same for the second ([1,:]) sequence but taking into account different sequence lengths ([1,:8])
emb_1 = embedding_repr.last_hidden_state[1,:8] # shape (8 x 1024)

# if you want to derive a single representation (per-protein embedding) for the whole protein
emb_0_per_protein = emb_0.mean(dim=0) # shape (1024)
PY
steps.explanation: The README quick start, wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads the encoder-only checkpoint and computes embeddings for two short example sequences.

outputs: Per-residue embeddings of shape 7 x 1024 and 8 x 1024 for the two example sequences, and a 1024-value per-protein embedding for the first, held in memory. The snippet prints nothing.
